Box structures

Rigid boxes or folding cartons?

FORME Packaging editorialUpdated October 21, 20263 min read

A wrapped rigid box and a white-card folding carton are different constructions. Compare material thickness, closure, packing and the role the packaging plays in the complete product system.

In this guideRecognize the material and constructionChoose the closure for the contentsCompare the complete packaging systemUse each format where it adds valueDiscuss your packaging →

Recognize the material and construction

A setup rigid box is formed from relatively stiff board and commonly wrapped with a decorative paper. The wall shape remains established after assembly. A white-card folding carton is cut and creased from solid paperboard, then folded and glued into its finished form. Its thin edges and tuck flaps should remain visible in a realistic product image.

Corrugated board is a third construction: a fluted medium sits between liners. A die-cut corrugated mailer may fold flat, but it is not the same material as a solid white-card carton. Specify the actual board instead of using “cardboard” for all three.

Choose the closure for the contents

A folding carton may use straight-tuck or reverse-tuck ends, a lock-bottom construction or an auto-bottom structure. The choice depends on the product, dimensions and packing method. Do not assume a tuck-end carton can carry a heavy item without an appropriate support and bottom review.

Rigid formats use other actions, such as lift-off lids, connected magnetic covers or sliding drawers. An insert may still be necessary to support a bottle, jar or multi-item set.

Compare the complete packaging system

ConsiderationRigid presentationWhite-card carton
ConstructionFormed board with wrapPrinted, creased solid paperboard
Typical openingLid, drawer or hinged coverTuck flap or other folded closure
StorageUsually assembled; collapsible variants existOften supplied flat
Product supportFitted inserts and partitionsFolded inserts and suitable bottom design

Use each format where it adds value

A retail skincare bottle may use a printed folding carton, while a coordinated launch set uses a rigid presentation around several individually boxed products. Both can then travel inside a corrugated shipping case. Thinking in layers avoids asking one structure to do every job.

Review the white-card range alongside the rigid catalog. Confirm stock, dimensions, closure and a filled sample before deciding on a production format.
